observation.visible_scene: An outdoor garden scene with a large pile of dry brown branches, twigs and fallen leaves burning in the foreground. Behind the pile on the left is a low structure with a red-tiled roof and a small pale chimney/pipe; to the right and in the background are green grass and leafy shrubs. A separate blackened, charred mound sits to the right of the main pile, with smaller flames on it. A column of pale smoke rises from the center/right of the fire.
visible_changes: Flames across the pile flicker and change shape continuously from frame to frame, with no single ignition or extinction event inside the clip.
The tall central flame column varies in height and brightness, e.g. lower and broader in early frames, taller and more concentrated in mid frames.
Small flames on the right-hand charred mound wax and wane, sometimes forming a taller tongue (around frames 17-21) and sometimes shrinking to low licks.
The rising smoke plume drifts upward and slightly to the right and appears denser/more diffuse in the later frames than in the first few.

The unburned brown leaf/branch pile on the left and the charred mound on the right keep essentially the same outline and position throughout; visible change is in the fire and smoke, not in the bulk of the fuel.
Background (roof, shrubs, grass) stays in fixed positions, indicating the camera is essentially static with at most minor handheld shake.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was started, and whether it is later extinguished or grows beyond this segment.
The full size of the fuel pile and what lies outside the frame.
Whether ambient wind is driving the smoke drift and flame flicker.
uncertain_details: Whether the overall fire intensity is genuinely increasing or the apparent smoke thickening is just flicker/drift.
Exact material of the burning pile (garden trimmings/wood) is inferred from appearance only.
Minor apparent camera jitter vs. true motion is hard to separate given the static background.
